title: MOVAPS — Move Aligned Packed Single Precision Floating-Point Values
why: Verifies the lab's 128-bit aligned memory store and its general-protection exception on misalignment.

title: Go runtime cgo call and callback support
why: Documents generated wrappers and runtime adapters on both Go-to-C and C-to-Go crossings.

claim: A 128-bit MOVAPS memory operand must be 16-byte aligned or the instruction raises a general-protection exception.
quote: When the source or destination operand is a memory operand, the operand must be aligned on a 16-byte boundary or a general-protection exception (#GP) will be generated.

claim: In 64-bit mode the operand size of a near call is forced to 64 bits.
quote: When in 64-bit mode, the operand size for near call (and all near branches) is forced to 64-bits.

claim: A 64-bit near relative call pushes RIP as an eight-byte return address.
CMP subtracts its second Intel-syntax operand from its first and sets flags in the same manner as SUB.
quote: The comparison is performed by subtracting the second operand from the first operand and then setting the status flags in the same manner as the SUB instruction.

claim: ZF indicates a zero result, and SF equals the result's most-significant bit.
quote: ZF (bit 6) Zero flag — Set if the result is zero; cleared otherwise. SF (bit 7) Sign flag — Set equal to the most-significant bit of the result, which is the sign bit of a signed integer.

claim: CF indicates a carry or borrow out of the result's most-significant bit and unsigned arithmetic overflow.
quote: CF (bit 0) Carry flag — Set if an arithmetic operation generates a carry or a borrow out of the most-significant bit of the result; cleared otherwise. This flag indicates an overflow condition for unsigned-integer arithmetic.

claim: OF indicates that a signed integer result does not fit in its destination.
quote: OF (bit 11) Overflow flag — Set if the integer result is too large a positive number or too small a negative number (excluding the sign-bit) to fit in the destination operand; cleared otherwise. This flag indicates an overflow condition for signed-integer (two’s complement) arithmetic.

locator: Function call argument and result passing
claim: Go's internal ABI passes arguments and results in registers when eligible, and otherwise on the stack.
quote: Function calls pass arguments and results using a combination of the stack and machine registers. Each argument or result is passed either entirely in registers or entirely on the stack.

claim: A cgo-generated C wrapper takes arguments from a frame structure and writes the C function's results back into it.
The cgo callback path uses crosscall2 as an adapter from the C compiler's function-call ABI to Go's.
quote:
crosscall2 (in cgo/asm_$GOARCH.s) is a four-argument adapter from
// the gcc function call ABI to the gc function call ABI.

locator: section 3.5.1 Instruction Pointer in 64-Bit Mode, p. 3-18
claim: RIP is the 64-bit instruction pointer and holds the offset of the next instruction.
quote: In 64-bit mode, the RIP register becomes the instruction pointer. This register holds the 64-bit offset of the next instruction to be executed.

claim: The lower 16 bits of the original general-purpose registers retain the names of the 8086 and Intel 286 registers.
quote: As shown in Figure 3-5, the lower 16 bits of the general-purpose registers map directly to the register set found in the 8086 and Intel 286 processors and can be referenced with the names AX, BX, CX, DX, BP, SI, DI, and SP.

locator: section 3.4.1.1 General-Purpose Registers in 64-Bit Mode, p. 3-12
claim: R8 through R15 are eight new general-purpose registers available in 64-bit mode.
quote: R8D-R15D/R8-R15 represent eight new general-purpose registers.

claim: The scale in an x86 memory operand multiplies the index and can be 1, 2, 4, or 8.
quote: scale, taking the values 1, 2, 4, and 8, multiplies index to calculate the address of the operand.

claim: Windows x64 uses RCX, RDX, R8, and R9 for integer arguments in the first four argument positions, not the first four integer arguments regardless of position.
quote: Integer valued arguments in the leftmost four positions are passed in left-to-right order in RCX, RDX, R8, and R9, respectively.

claim: GCC's frame-pointer omission option applies to functions that do not need a frame pointer.
quote: Omit the frame pointer in functions that don’t need one.

claim: MOV r32, imm32 uses opcode B8+rd and a 32-bit immediate, whereas MOV r64, imm64 additionally uses REX.W and a 64-bit immediate.
quote:
| B8+ rd id         | MOV r32, imm32         | OI    | Valid       | Valid           | Move imm32 to r32.                                         |
| REX.W + B8+ rd io | MOV r64, imm64         | OI    | Valid       | N.E.            | Move imm64 to r64.                                         |
